Commentary.Commentary: Here we go! Sri Lanka walk out to chase 209 in 50 overs. Avishka Fernando and the skipper Kusal Mendis are out to open the batting. Richard Ngarava to start the attack for Zimbabwe. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka showcased a commendable effort with the ball and in the field, restricting Zimbabwe to a competitive yet achievable total. The captain Kusal Mendis, used 8 bowlers in the innings and maintained an attacking and economical approach throughout the innings. Maheesh Theekshana impressed with a haul of 4 wickets, while Dushmantha Chameera's brilliant spell in the third phase dismantled the set batters, Ervine and Ryan Burl, turning the tide in Sri Lanka's favor. As the Sri Lankan batting lineup prepares to chase down the target of 209 runs, the stage is set for an intriguing second innings. The question remains: Will they be able to achieve the target with finesse? The answer awaits in what promises to be an exciting and closely contested encounter. Stay tuned as the run chase is coming up.

The first innings of the second ODI between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe concludes, with Zimbabwe setting a target of 209 runs after opting to bat first. Despite a challenging start, losing their first wicket in the opening over, Zimbabwe's skipper Craig Ervine played a crucial role in stabilizing the innings. Ervine, along with Joylord Gumble, forged a 60-run partnership for the second wicket. Ervine's standout performance saw him scoring 82 runs off 102 balls, with nine boundaries and a brilliant six over covers, steering the innings until the 35th over. However, after his dismissal, Zimbabwe experienced a collapse which saw them lose their last six wickets for just 26 runs, ultimately finishing their innings at 208.

The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the Sri Lankan players who spread out and take their respective field positions.  Joylord Gumbie and Tinashe Kamunhukamwe are the two openers for Zimbabwe. Dilshan Madushanka has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Kusal Mendis, the captain of Sri Lanka says he is happy with the decision as the weather is a bit cloudy. He praises the way Charith Asalanka played in the last game and Sadeera Samarawickrama also supported him well for the partnership. He hopes that his batters bat the same way in this match. Informs they are unchanged.

Craig Ervine, the skipper of Zimbabwe says that they will bat first. Adds it looks like a good wicket and they have seen the ball do a bit under lights and want to capitalise on it. Tells that the players have been hydrating well after the previous game and we hope they don't find any injuries this time around. Informs Joylord Gumbie comes in for Takudzwanashe Kaitano. Ends by saying the lads are fit and ready to perform.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is pitchside. He says that the wicket is a different one from the first game but with a similar quality. Adds the batting conditions look good as the wicket is hard and well-prepared. Tells there are a few clouds in the background, but the game is going to start, and hopes for a result here. Ends by saying the wicket here has always been good for the captain to win and bat first

Zimbabwe have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

On the other hand, it was a pity for Zimbabwe as their bowlers did a pretty good job restricting the Lankans despite a few of them having injury issues. The rain gods showed no mercy on them and poured water on their valuable efforts. While chasing, their batters looked unsettled and they will have to improve that and release some pressure from Sikandar Raza as he cannot take them over the line single-handedly every time. Let's hope the weather gets cleared up and we can at least get a result here. Toss and team news in a bit.

The first match of this three-match ODI series was a washout as rain played spoilsport. The hosts failed to put up a good score against the Zimbabwean bowling unit. Sadeera Samarawickrama and Kusal Mendis started off things pretty well but no one other than the vice-captain, Charith Asalanka, stood up as he registered a fine ton. However, they would hope that in this game, the other batters take more responsibility as their bowling looked pretty solid in the four overs that were possible before rain halted proceedings in that game.

After a lucky escape for Zimbabwe in the first game with rain taking center stage, the hosts Sri Lanka take on the visitors Zimbabwe in the 2nd ODI at the R.Premadasa Stadium, Colombo. The bowlers had a lovely outing in the first game till it lasted with both sets of bowlers enjoying the purchase from the surface. It was an outstanding innings of 101 from Charith Asalanka on a tricky surface that saw the Lankans post 273 in their 50 overs. Other batters of Sri Lanka did get some start barring Avishka Fernando but couldn't build up on that and failed to go big. Chasing down the total set by the Lankans, Zimbabwe were 2 down on 12 after 4 when rain played the spoilsport. Richard Ngarava though was carried off due to suffering cramps regularly. The hosts would be looking for some more clinical performance with the bat in the 2nd ODI while the visitors would be looking to improve on their batting as well. Both sides would be hoping they get a full game this time around. Expect a close contest when these two sides collide for the 2nd time in the 3-match ODI series.
